text:
alex: heads up — eu-west gpu pool (racks r12-r14) showing 18% of nodes stuck in provisioning after last night's BMC microcode rollout. some of them have secure-boot toggled to "unknown" and OOB routes are asymmetric.

maya: which rack/range exactly? any common BMC version?

alex: r12-r14, about 9 hosts total. looks like mix of bmc v2.1.4 and v2.2.0. deploy-bot posted the rollout at 02:12 UTC. ops-bot alert pasted below.

ops-bot: [ALERT] firmware-rollout eu-west: bmc-microcode v2.2.0 -> 2.2.1 started for racks r10-r15 at 2025-02-11T02:12Z

cj: can you paste the OOB route table from one of the stuck hosts? suspect asymmetric default-gateway via jump host.

alex: here's `ipmitool lan print` from host r13-045 (redacted):

```
IP Address              : 10.40.13.45
Subnet Mask             : 255.255.255.0
Default Gateway IP      : 10.40.13.1
MAC Address             : 5c:26:0a:xx:xx:xx
BMC Version             : 2.2.0
Secure Boot             : disabled
```

alex: and from r13-052 (stuck):

```
IP Address              : 10.40.13.52
Default Gateway IP      : 192.168.99.1   # <-- odd
BMC Version             : 2.1.4
Secure Boot             : unknown
```

raj: that gateway jump looks wrong — some nodes picked up old mgmt-subnet via fallback when the new jump-host route was created. run `oobctl check-route --rack r13` and `oobctl show-bmc-version --rack r13`

alex: ran checks, output snippet:

```
$ oobctl check-route --rack r13
r13-045 -> gw 10.40.13.1 (ok)
r13-052 -> gw 192.168.99.1 (via jumphost-legacy) (mismatch)
```

maya: if the BMCs are on different mgmt vlans they may not see the KMS/HSM attestation endpoint which flips secureboot state during microcode update. that explains unknown secure boot and provisioning timeout.

lena: this is on Dedicated capacity, losing 9 GPUs reduces capacity for current customers. we need a mitigation path ASAP — potential SLA impact and cost for fallback allocation.

cj: mitigation idea: temporarily reroute jumphost-legacy traffic to the new mgmt subnet OR pin affected hosts to previous microcode and mark them as non-provisionable for canary traffic. prefer reroute first to avoid rollbacks.

raj: runbook to try (quick):
1) `oobctl route-redirect --src 192.168.99.0/24 --dst 10.40.13.0/24 --rack r13`
2) `oobctl watchdog-reset --hosts r13-05[0-9]`
3) if secureboot still unknown, `bmcctl set-secureboot --host <host> --state enabled|disabled` (requires KMS access)

alex: started step 1 now. routing change applied to jumphost-legacy via edge-rt1. will watch.

[~00:45 later]

alex: routing redirect applied. five hosts moved to correct gateway. three still showing secure-boot unknown and two still timing out on provisioning. ran `bmcctl show` on one: 

```
$ bmcctl show r13-052
Host: r13-052
BMC Version: 2.1.4
Provisioning: stalled (kv-cache timeout)
SecureBoot: unknown
LastAttest: 2025-02-11T02:30:18Z status=fallback
```

maya: sounds like those BMCs never completed attestation step during the roll. we should avoid a mass reboot. do per-host controlled reboot + reattest. tag for SRE oncall. @oncall-sre could you take the three hosts for controlled remediation?

oncall-sre: oncall-sre: taking r13-050, r13-052, r13-058. will perform controlled reboots and monitor attestation logs.

cj: if reattest fails, fallback is to roll back microcode on those hosts to 2.1.4 and reprovision. add a note: rollback will temporarily avoid secureboot attestation and force fresh provisioning.

lena: please create an incident ticket, include capacity impact estimate and customer list for Dedicated nodes. also need cost estimate for fallback capacity (eg spin up cloud fallback nodes for 48h).

alex: creating incident now and will attach these logs. incident-1234 created. assigning to infra oncall + solutions-eng.

deploy-bot: [INFO] firmware-rollout eu-west paused at 2025-02-11T03:05Z due to manual intervention on racks r12-r14

alex: quick postmortem note — probable root cause: mixed BMC microcode + asymmetrical OOB routing + KMS attestation unavailable on legacy jump-host subnet during rollout. remediation steps: fix routing, limit parallelism on microcode rollouts per rack, add preflight check for attestation endpoint reachability.

maya: agree. also add a verification step to bail early if >5% nodes report secureboot unknown after patch.

cj: +1 to preflight and lower parallelism. also we should tag microcode as compatible-only-if attestation reachable.

lena: thanks everyone. tagging support and customer success to prepare comms. :thumbsup:

alex: will add timeline and follow-up runbook to the incident. :white_check_mark:
